{{short description|Fourier expansion of a reciprocal square root}}

In [[mathematical analysis]], '''Heine's identity''', named after [[Eduard Heine]],{{sfnp|Heine|1881|p=[https://historical.library.cornell.edu/cgi-bin/cul.math/docviewer?did=01410002&seq=&view=50&frames=0&pagenum=286 286]}} is a [[Fourier expansion]] of a [[Reciprocal (mathematics)|reciprocal]] [[square root]]:{{sfnp|Cohl|Tohline|Rau|Srivastava|2000}}
:<math>\frac{1}{\sqrt{z-\cos\psi}} = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{\pi}\sum_{m=-\infty}^\infty Q_{m-\frac12}(z) e^{im\psi},</math>
where <math>Q_{m-1/2}</math> is a [[Legendre function#Legendre function of the second kind (Qn)|Legendre function of the second kind]] and <math>z\in\R_{>1}</math>. This expression can be generalized for arbitrary half-integer powers as follows:{{sfnp|Cohl|2003}}
:<math>(z-\cos\psi)^{n-\frac12} = \sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}}\frac{(z^2-1)^{\frac{n}{2}}}{\Gamma(\frac12-n)}
\sum_{m=-\infty}^{\infty} \frac{\Gamma(m-n+\frac12)}{\Gamma(m+n+\frac12)}Q_{m-\frac12}^n(z)e^{im\psi},</math>
where <math>\Gamma</math> is the [[gamma function]].
